targets.authors: Carollo A, Bizzego A, Gabrieli G, Wong KKY, Raine A, Esposito G.
targets.title: I’m alone but not lonely. U-shaped pattern of self-perceived loneliness during the COVID-19 pandemic in the UK and Greece.
targets.evidence_quote: In the second part, the study aims to test whether the documented distribution of self-perceived loneliness levels by week in lockdown depended on the specific wave of lockdown.
targets.outcome_quote: These results have to be considered only as a qualitative and preliminary insight, as the sample size collected for the weeks of interest did not allow any meaningful statistical inference to be made. In fact, graphical disparities among scores might be mere random variation and they might not reflect real differences.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The new Wave 2 test is explicitly unable to support meaningful inference; a qualitative U shape does not override that adjudicative limitation.

reasoning: The paper combines a robustness reanalysis of Wave 1 with a new Wave 2 sample re-testing the earlier published loneliness result. Record type follows the new-sample replication. Alternative models on the original data select depression rather than loneliness, but the replication verdict concerns Wave 2. Only Carollo et al. reference 19 is actually re-tested.
